Two families bind committed records by exact SHA-256 and I rehashed every one: national-report-batch-b.json to 883d5bb8… at 25265 bytes, and 2026-08-28-national-legal-decisions.json to 0aad88ef… at 184365 bytes — both matching their receipts exactly. forTheCaptain.item: The § 61-11-26(o) once-per-lifetime question is unanswered in the packet.
forTheCaptain.detail: WV.memo.json records it as a release_blocker on eligibility_branch, with the reasoning that 'a participant deciding whether to spend their one lifetime conviction petition needs the right answer'. The packet states the different, internal § 17C-5-2b(e) limit — only one discharge and dismissal, ever — which a reader could easily mistake for the same limit. I did not score this as a failure of any of the fifteen, because it is an open legal question and the review model puts counsel review after state_built. It is the one substantive participant-facing gap I found in this batch and it will need an answer before approved_for_live.

forTheCaptain.detail: NE.memo.json's legalDesignDecision recommends OVERRIDING the controlling legal review's classification of this route as outside self-help scope, and states in terms that the override must be counsel-confirmed. Two further release_blockers stand open: Nebraska mandamus procedure was not surveyed, and the rule for service on a public body was not surveyed. The packet discloses all three to the participant honestly, which is why the obligations pass — but a Captain should see that the route's very existence as a self-help product is an unconfirmed override rather than a settled reading.
